text:
repo_admin_jane: Hey team, our finance lead spotted a small but odd gap on the May invoice for acct `acme-corp` — dashboard usage (tokens) matches expected, but the invoice total is off by £0.03 after conversion to GBP from USD. Can someone look?

emma_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the invoice snippet and the dashboard totals?

repo_admin_jane: Invoice lines (excerpt):
```
2026-05-31 | model:txl-v1 | 1,234,567 tokens | Unit price $0.0008 | Subtotal $987.65
2026-05-31 | embeddings | 12,345 units | Unit price $0.0100 | Subtotal $123.45
Tax (VAT @20%): $222.62
Grand total: $1,333.72
Converted to GBP @1.25 = £1,066.98
```
Dashboard shows raw USD subtotal $1,111.10 and when converted the math should be £888.88 (not matching). We see a -£0.03 residual on the printed GBP invoice total vs sum of rounded line items.

josh_billing: Thanks — can you share the invoice_id and the conversion rate logged on the invoice meta? Also did you have a manual credit or promo applied?

repo_admin_jane: invoice_id INV-2026-05-0198, no promo. Conversion rate on invoice meta: 1.25 (USD->GBP).

marta_finance: Quick note: finance requires the per-line rounding method used (round half up vs bankers rounding) — small differences add up when we aggregate many line items.

vikram_backend: Repro steps I ran: 1) Pull usage rows for acct `acme-corp` for May. 2) Aggregate tokens, compute USD prices per item with full precision. 3) Apply VAT on final USD sum, then convert whole to GBP, then round to 2 decimals -> yields a different result than converting each per-line amount to GBP and then rounding per-line. Looks like invoicing pipeline converts each per-line subtotal to GBP and rounds them, then sums, which can create +/- a few pence.

kevin_sre: @vikram can you paste the SQL you ran so billing can compare?

vikram_backend: SQL I used: ```
SELECT usage_type, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(tokens*unit_price) as usd_subtotal
FROM usage_rows
WHERE account_id='acme-corp' AND date >= '2026-05-01' AND date <= '2026-05-31'
GROUP BY usage_type;
```
Then `total_usd = SUM(usd_subtotal)`; `vat_usd = total_usd * 0.2`; `grand_usd = total_usd + vat_usd`; `grand_gbp = grand_usd / 1.25` and round to 2 decimals at end.

josh_billing: Confirmed: current production invoice job instead converts each line to customer currency (USD->GBP) using the stored fx rate per invoice row, rounds each line to 2 decimals, then sums them, and also computes VAT on the already-rounded per-line totals. That's different from how the dashboard aggregates (full-precision USD -> VAT -> convert once). Both are reasonable but produce different tiny residuals.

marta_finance: From a finance compliance POV we need invoice numbers to match the sum of lines shown on PDF. Small negative residuals (like -£0.03) are bad.

emma_support: Customer thread says they want an explanation and either an adjustment or a clear note on the invoice. Can we patch the invoice generator to carry a residual line item ("Rounding adjustment") instead of letting grand total drift?

josh_billing: Short-term: we can add a line item labelled "Rounding adjustment" to force line-sum == grand total. I'll open a billing ticket to add that for invoices where abs(residual) >= £0.01. Long-term: we should standardize to one canonical rounding strategy — finance prefers compute VAT in GBP after conversion and then round, or vice versa? Marta?

marta_finance: Preference: compute VAT in customer currency (GBP) after converting the full-precision USD grand total, then round final VAT and totals. That minimizes visible residuals on GBP invoices. Please propose change and I'll approve.

vikram_backend: Tech note: changing rounding strategy is a behavior change that will affect all historical invoices if we backfill. We should only change future invoices and document the policy. Also will add a deterministic "rounding_adjustment" field in DB so we can show it on PDFs via invoice template.

kevin_sre: Also logging request: add invoice-level debug blob to S3 for each generated invoice with pre-rounding figures so support can reproduce easily.

invoice_bot: Invoice generator job finished for INV-2026-05-0198: added rounding_adjustment = -0.03 GBP as requested by billing. PDF regenerated.

repo_admin_jane: Thanks — customer confirmed they received updated PDF and appreciates the explanation. Can we add a small footnote on invoices about rounding ("All conversions use FX rate X and line items may be rounded to two decimals; a rounding adjustment line may be present").

marta_finance: Good idea. I'll add text for legal review.

emma_support: I'll reply to the customer summarizing cause, the fix (adjustment line), and the timeline for the policy change.

repo_admin_jane: Closing this thread for now, please link the billing ticket to INV-2026-05-0198 in the ticketing system. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
